BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. === SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Executive view

The Seller’s package materially departs from the Buyer playbook. The statements that provisions are “standard”, “final”, “settled at principal level” or “cleared by both sides” are unsupported counterparty assertions and do not establish Buyer approval. In particular, no written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for the proposed 20% cap or 18-month claims period.

The most important pushbacks are:

1. Restore the Buyer’s liability package: 25% general cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket and 24 months.
2. Establish a separate 100%/six-year regime for title and fundamental matters.
3. Carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of every contractual protection.
4. Reject data-room/public-record deemed disclosure and blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusions.
5. Make effective Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of its conditions, a genuine condition precedent.
6. Repay Riverlark directly at Completion and obtain effective security releases.
7. Expressly allocate the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all applicable on-costs to the Seller.
8. Broaden the Ironquay protection and independently verify the asserted AUD 180,000.
9. Preserve and investigate the export/privacy evidence without assuming either a breach or no material exposure.
10. Keep title, tax, IP, payment, covenant and specific-indemnity claims outside any hidden general-regime override.

## Detailed review

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Departure:** The Buyer’s authorised starting position is 25%, or AUD 6 million. Although 20% matches a possible fallback, that fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the relevant draft. No such authority exists.

**Pushback:** Reinstate a **25% / AUD 6 million** general Warranty Claim cap. Do not treat the numerical match to the fallback as approval.

The clause must also make clear that the general cap does not govern:

- title, ownership, capacity or authority claims;
- Tax Claims, pending separate agreement;
- specific IP indemnities, including Ironquay;
- payment obligations and purchase-price adjustments;
- Completion and post-Completion covenants;
- fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; only losses above the basket are recoverable.

**Departure:** Every element is contrary to the playbook:

- de minimis should be **AUD 5,000**;
- basket should be **AUD 50,000**;
- it should be a **tipping basket**, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

The Seller’s proposal would disregard smaller but legitimate claims and leave the Buyer permanently bearing the first AUD 250,000.

**Pushback:** Restore the playbook thresholds and expressly exclude fundamental/title, fraud and specific indemnity claims from both thresholds.

### 3. General claims period

**Seller position:** 18 months.

**Departure:** The authorised position is **24 months after Completion**. Eighteen months is only a fallback requiring Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been provided.

**Pushback:** Reinstate 24 months. Ensure timely notification preserves a claim rather than requiring final resolution or commencement of proceedings within the notification period.

### 4. Fundamental and title claims

**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties would be subject to the general cap and general time limit.

**Departure:** This directly contradicts the required separate regime. It would potentially cap defective ownership of the shares at AUD 4.8 million and extinguish the claim after 18 months.

**Pushback:** Provide that title, ownership, encumbrance, capacity and authority claims have:

- a **100% purchase-price cap**;
- a period of **at least six years**;
- no general basket or de minimis;
- no Buyer-knowledge exclusion;
- no limitation based on data-room disclosure or non-reliance.

Title and capacity should be expressly identified rather than left to an uncertain definition of “Fundamental Warranty”.

### 5. Fraud and intentional wrongdoing

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims “of any nature”.

**Departure:** This could purport to protect the Seller against fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. That is prohibited by the playbook.

**Pushback:** Add an overriding provision, applying notwithstanding anything else in the SPA, that fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are excluded from:

- caps;
- baskets and de minimis;
- time limits;
- exclusive-remedy provisions;
- non-reliance language;
- Buyer-knowledge qualifications;
- disclosure protections,

in each case to the maximum extent enforceable.

The carve-out should not be undermined by a narrow definition of fraud or by requiring that the conduct be committed only by the Seller entity itself.

### 6. Hidden application of the general regime

The proposal that limitations applying to “Claims” apply to all claims unless expressly excluded is unacceptable. It creates a risk that the general cap, thresholds and time limit override separately negotiated protections.

**Pushback:** Use an affirmative claims matrix or express exclusions. Keep separate treatment for:

- general Warranty Claims;
- title/fundamental claims;
- Tax Claims;
- IP and other specific indemnities;
- payment obligations;
- price adjustments;
- Completion and other covenants;
- fraud and intentional wrongdoing.

Tax and IP are **open**, not “settled”. We should not accept either unlimited liability or the Seller’s proposed general regime without substantive review and agreement.

### 7. General disclosure of the data room and public records

**Seller position:** Everything in the indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records is generally disclosed.

**Departure:** The playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

The proposed language transfers the risk of identifying significance, inconsistencies and contractual consequences to the Buyer. A fact should not qualify a warranty merely because it appears somewhere in a document.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general warranty qualifications.
- Permit only matters specifically disclosed against identified warranties.
- Require sufficient detail to identify the nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable implications of the matter.
- Require document references to precise folders/pages or clauses, not broad document ranges.
- State that disclosure of one matter does not qualify unrelated warranties unless expressly cross-referenced.
- Do not accept public-record or “discoverable by search” disclosure.

The specific items in paragraphs 2–10 may be considered individually, but their presence does not automatically amount to fair disclosure of every resulting breach or exposure.

The non-admission language in paragraph 1.4 can remain only as procedural language; it must not negate factual statements, limit the warranties or indemnities, or shift the agreed risk allocation.

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is much broader than actual knowledge and effectively recreates general deemed disclosure. It also attributes the knowledge of an undefined group of advisers to the Buyer.

**Pushback:** Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion. In particular:

- no constructive, imputed or “discoverable” knowledge;
- no attribution from all advisers;
- no knowledge limitation for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities;
- due diligence should not waive contractual protection unless a particular exception is specifically and fairly disclosed and expressly agreed.

Any Seller warranty qualified by Seller knowledge should use named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. The Seller should not be permitted to use vague corporate knowledge formulations.

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, around 30%. The final written consent and evidence of satisfaction of the associated conditions are absent.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** For a customer of this significance, reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient. Delivery of a document does not establish that the consent is effective or that its conditions have been met.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional on:

- valid and effective written Bluefen consent;
- consent in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer;
- satisfaction or valid waiver of every associated condition;
- evidence of satisfaction or waiver delivered before Completion;
- no adverse amendment, termination right, price change or other material condition imposed on the Company.

Reasonable endeavours may operate as an interim Seller covenant but not as a substitute for the condition precedent. The Buyer should control whether any onerous condition is acceptable.

### 10. Riverlark debt and security

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; it has not been repaid and no final discharge is included.

**Seller position:** Release following Completion.

**Departure:** This conflicts with a debt-free/cash-free transaction and leaves the Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security after acquiring the Company.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an up-to-date payout letter covering principal, interest, fees and break costs;
- direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
- effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security at Completion;
- evidence enabling prompt registration of releases on relevant registers;
- a funds-flow line item and payment direction agreed before Completion.

A post-Completion release is unacceptable unless supported by an irrevocable bank undertaking and separately approved in writing by Amelia Frost. No such approval presently exists.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses are not included in the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs have not been quantified.

**Seller position:** The bonuses are “a matter for the Seller” but are not separately itemised.

**Risk:** That formulation does not prevent the Company—and therefore the Buyer after Completion—from paying them. The omission could also distort the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

**Pushback:** Before signing or Completion:

- quantify bonuses and all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs;
- include them as an express funds-flow line item or otherwise require full Seller funding;
- prohibit payment from post-Completion Company cash unless reimbursed dollar-for-dollar;
- obtain evidence of payment and satisfaction of associated withholding and reporting obligations;
- clarify treatment if an employee fails the continued-employment condition.

The SPA should allocate the liability expressly rather than rely on narrative assurances.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but this is not independent bank verification. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is available.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** The Buyer’s exposure is not merely the payment amount. It includes failure of title or transfer, licence limitations, infringement or third-party claims, operational remediation and the cost of obtaining replacement rights.

**Pushback:**

- Independently verify whether the AUD 180,000 is due, paid or disputed.
- Require payment/cure and an effective transfer or confirmatory assignment before Completion where possible.
- Preserve the existing SOW3 cure mechanism.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from failure to obtain the contracted Project Materials and associated IP rights, Ironquay claims, infringement exposure and reasonable cure/remediation costs.
- Prevent this indemnity from being absorbed into the general cap, basket or 24-month period.

We should not assert either that AUD 180,000 is definitely owed or that payment alone fully cures the IP issue.

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A link was sent to an unintended external address and may have contained approximately 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification requirements are unresolved.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** “Not expected to be material” is unsupported. Equally, the evidence does not establish a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or loss amount.

**Pushback:** Require the Seller and Company to:

- preserve emails, access logs, download logs, system records and investigation materials;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- provide regular written updates and promptly disclose material developments;
- take reasonable containment and remediation steps;
- consult the Buyer before external notifications or admissions, subject to legal requirements;
- notify the Buyer immediately of evidence of access, misuse, regulatory contact or a notification obligation;
- avoid destroying or overwriting relevant records.

The SPA and disclosure response should remain neutral on whether a notifiable breach or loss has occurred. Any indemnity or retention decision should follow better factual assessment rather than an invented numeric demand.

### 14. Sandbar renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three related renewals total AUD 330,000, but the documents do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That characterisation is not established by the disclosure. Conversely, the amount should not automatically be treated as Debt or deducted from price.

**Pushback:** Obtain and review the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, invoicing and accrual status, service periods and consistency with historical practice. Then decide whether the costs are:

- ordinary-course expenses;
- accrued liabilities reflected in working capital;
- commitments requiring specific disclosure; or
- exceptional items needing a separate adjustment.

### 15. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosed documents presently indicate:

- an office lease notification obligation, not necessarily landlord consent; and
- a Mossvale assignment restriction that may not be triggered by a share sale.

We should not manufacture consent requirements. However, the underlying clauses should be checked for change-of-control language, indirect assignment concepts, cross-defaults and prescribed notification timing. Any required notices should be included in the Completion plan.

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register is sufficient evidence of ownership.

**Departure:** DD-012 is an internal Company record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. It does not by itself establish beneficial ownership, valid issue and transfer history, absence of encumbrances or Seller authority.

**Pushback:** Require independent verification, including as appropriate:

- ASIC and PPSR searches;
- original or verified share certificates;
- issue and transfer records and relevant board approvals;
- constitution and shareholders’ agreements;
- evidence of discharge of any share security;
- Seller corporate authority and execution approvals;
- confirmation that no options, convertibles or third-party rights exist;
- Completion delivery of registrable transfers and updated registers.

This diligence complements, rather than replaces, the title warranties and 100% liability regime.

### 17. Disclosure cut-off and factual refresh

The Disclosure Letter is stated as at **5.00 pm on 22 September 2026**, while the current review occurs later. That record is stale for matters such as Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, the Ironquay balance, employee conditions and the incident investigation.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an updated data-room index;
- refreshed disclosures and supporting documents;
- confirmation of changes since 22 September;
- a bring-down of warranties and disclosures at Completion;
- Buyer consent to material supplemental disclosures rather than automatic qualification of warranties.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Non-negotiable or authority-controlled points

- Reject the 20% cap absent Amelia Frost’s written approval; propose 25%.
- Reject 18 months absent Amelia Frost’s written approval; propose 24 months.
- Require 100%/six-year title and fundamental protection.
- Preserve the absolute fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
- Reject post-Completion Riverlark release unless the required irrevocable undertaking and Amelia approval are obtained.

### Priority closing protections

- Effective Bluefen consent with all conditions satisfied.
- Riverlark repayment and effective releases at Completion.
- Seller-funded bonuses and on-costs expressly included in funds flow.
- Ironquay cure, transfer evidence and broader indemnity.
- Updated investigation and evidence-preservation obligations for DD-006.
- Independent title and encumbrance verification.

### Drafting architecture

- Restore AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
- Delete general data-room/public-record disclosure.
- Delete blanket Buyer-knowledge language.
- Prevent general limitations from applying automatically to title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payments and covenants.
- Keep Tax and IP positions expressly open pending substantive agreement.
- Refresh the disclosure record through signing and Completion.

The proposed language transfers the risk of identifying significance, inconsistencies and contractual consequences to the Buyer. A fact should not qualify a warranty merely because it appears somewhere in a document.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general warranty qualifications.
- Permit only matters specifically disclosed against identified warranties.
- Require sufficient detail to identify the nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable implications of the matter.
- Require document references to precise folders/pages or clauses, not broad document ranges.
- State that disclosure of one matter does not qualify unrelated warranties unless expressly cross-referenced.
- Do not accept public-record or “discoverable by search” disclosure.

The specific items in paragraphs 2–10 may be considered individually, but their presence does not automatically amount to fair disclosure of every resulting breach or exposure.

The non-admission language in paragraph 1.4 can remain only as procedural language; it must not negate factual statements, limit the warranties or indemnities, or shift the agreed risk allocation.

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is much broader than actual knowledge and effectively recreates general deemed disclosure. It also attributes the knowledge of an undefined group of advisers to the Buyer.

**Pushback:** Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion. In particular:

- no constructive, imputed or “discoverable” knowledge;
- no attribution from all advisers;
- no knowledge limitation for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities;
- due diligence should not waive contractual protection unless a particular exception is specifically and fairly disclosed and expressly agreed.

Any Seller warranty qualified by Seller knowledge should use named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. The Seller should not be permitted to use vague corporate knowledge formulations.

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, around 30%. The final written consent and evidence of satisfaction of the associated conditions are absent.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** For a customer of this significance, reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient. Delivery of a document does not establish that the consent is effective or that its conditions have been met.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional on:

- valid and effective written Bluefen consent;
- consent in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer;
- satisfaction or valid waiver of every associated condition;
- evidence of satisfaction or waiver delivered before Completion;
- no adverse amendment, termination right, price change or other material condition imposed on the Company.

Reasonable endeavours may operate as an interim Seller covenant but not as a substitute for the condition precedent. The Buyer should control whether any onerous condition is acceptable.

### 10. Riverlark debt and security

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; it has not been repaid and no final discharge is included.

**Seller position:** Release following Completion.

**Departure:** This conflicts with a debt-free/cash-free transaction and leaves the Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security after acquiring the Company.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an up-to-date payout letter covering principal, interest, fees and break costs;
- direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
- effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security at Completion;
- evidence enabling prompt registration of releases on relevant registers;
- a funds-flow line item and payment direction agreed before Completion.

A post-Completion release is unacceptable unless supported by an irrevocable bank undertaking and separately approved in writing by Amelia Frost. No such approval presently exists.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses are not included in the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs have not been quantified.

**Seller position:** The bonuses are “a matter for the Seller” but are not separately itemised.

**Risk:** That formulation does not prevent the Company—and therefore the Buyer after Completion—from paying them. The omission could also distort the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

**Pushback:** Before signing or Completion:

- quantify bonuses and all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs;
- include them as an express funds-flow line item or otherwise require full Seller funding;
- prohibit payment from post-Completion Company cash unless reimbursed dollar-for-dollar;
- obtain evidence of payment and satisfaction of associated withholding and reporting obligations;
- clarify treatment if an employee fails the continued-employment condition.

The SPA should allocate the liability expressly rather than rely on narrative assurances.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but this is not independent bank verification. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is available.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** The Buyer’s exposure is not merely the payment amount. It includes failure of title or transfer, licence limitations, infringement or third-party claims, operational remediation and the cost of obtaining replacement rights.

**Pushback:**

- Independently verify whether the AUD 180,000 is due, paid or disputed.
- Require payment/cure and an effective transfer or confirmatory assignment before Completion where possible.
- Preserve the existing SOW3 cure mechanism.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from failure to obtain the contracted Project Materials and associated IP rights, Ironquay claims, infringement exposure and reasonable cure/remediation costs.
- Prevent this indemnity from being absorbed into the general cap, basket or 24-month period.

We should not assert either that AUD 180,000 is definitely owed or that payment alone fully cures the IP issue.

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A link was sent to an unintended external address and may have contained approximately 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification requirements are unresolved.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** “Not expected to be material” is unsupported. Equally, the evidence does not establish a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or loss amount.

**Pushback:** Require the Seller and Company to:

- preserve emails, access logs, download logs, system records and investigation materials;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- provide regular written updates and promptly disclose material developments;
- take reasonable containment and remediation steps;
- consult the Buyer before external notifications or admissions, subject to legal requirements;
- notify the Buyer immediately of evidence of access, misuse, regulatory contact or a notification obligation;
- avoid destroying or overwriting relevant records.

The SPA and disclosure response should remain neutral on whether a notifiable breach or loss has occurred. Any indemnity or retention decision should follow better factual assessment rather than an invented numeric demand.

### 14. Sandbar renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three related renewals total AUD 330,000, but the documents do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That characterisation is not established by the disclosure. Conversely, the amount should not automatically be treated as Debt or deducted from price.

**Pushback:** Obtain and review the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, invoicing and accrual status, service periods and consistency with historical practice. Then decide whether the costs are:

- ordinary-course expenses;
- accrued liabilities reflected in working capital;
- commitments requiring specific disclosure; or
- exceptional items needing a separate adjustment.

### 15. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosed documents presently indicate:

- an office lease notification obligation, not necessarily landlord consent; and
- a Mossvale assignment restriction that may not be triggered by a share sale.

We should not manufacture consent requirements. However, the underlying clauses should be checked for change-of-control language, indirect assignment concepts, cross-defaults and prescribed notification timing. Any required notices should be included in the Completion plan.

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register is sufficient evidence of ownership.

**Departure:** DD-012 is an internal Company record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. It does not by itself establish beneficial ownership, valid issue and transfer history, absence of encumbrances or Seller authority.

**Pushback:** Require independent verification, including as appropriate:

- ASIC and PPSR searches;
- original or verified share certificates;
- issue and transfer records and relevant board approvals;
- constitution and shareholders’ agreements;
- evidence of discharge of any share security;
- Seller corporate authority and execution approvals;
- confirmation that no options, convertibles or third-party rights exist;
- Completion delivery of registrable transfers and updated registers.

This diligence complements, rather than replaces, the title warranties and 100% liability regime.

### 17. Disclosure cut-off and factual refresh

The Disclosure Letter is stated as at **5.00 pm on 22 September 2026**, while the current review occurs later. That record is stale for matters such as Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, the Ironquay balance, employee conditions and the incident investigation.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an updated data-room index;
- refreshed disclosures and supporting documents;
- confirmation of changes since 22 September;
- a bring-down of warranties and disclosures at Completion;
- Buyer consent to material supplemental disclosures rather than automatic qualification of warranties.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Non-negotiable or authority-controlled points

- Reject the 20% cap absent Amelia Frost’s written approval; propose 25%.
- Reject 18 months absent Amelia Frost’s written approval; propose 24 months.
- Require 100%/six-year title and fundamental protection.
- Preserve the absolute fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
- Reject post-Completion Riverlark release unless the required irrevocable undertaking and Amelia approval are obtained.

### Priority closing protections

- Effective Bluefen consent with all conditions satisfied.
- Riverlark repayment and effective releases at Completion.
- Seller-funded bonuses and on-costs expressly included in funds flow.
- Ironquay cure, transfer evidence and broader indemnity.
- Updated investigation and evidence-preservation obligations for DD-006.
- Independent title and encumbrance verification.

### Drafting architecture

- Restore AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
- Delete general data-room/public-record disclosure.
- Delete blanket Buyer-knowledge language.
- Prevent general limitations from applying automatically to title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payments and covenants.
- Keep Tax and IP positions expressly open pending substantive agreement.
- Refresh the disclosure record through signing and Completion.
